title: provenance-post's not-published warning wording depends on whether the publish job succeeded
description: LCLI-628 reviewer finding F4 (#357, 2026-09-28), deferred because it needs a release.yml edit. When the publish job is green, a not-published outcome can only be read-API lag (LCLI-460), after the read-back step already timed out with its own warning (release.yml:1378). But the warning still leads with 'The likely cause is a PARTIAL PUBLISH' and prescribes 'Re-run failed jobs'. Fix: pass needs.publish.result into --post and choose the lead cause from it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: provenance-post's not-published warning leads with read-API lag (LCLI-460) when the publish job succeeded, and with a partial publish only when it did not, by passing needs.publish.result into release-provenance.mjs --post
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0; reviewer pass on the scripts/ and release.yml change

plan: 1. Add --publish-result <success|failure|cancelled|skipped> to scripts/release-provenance.mjs: required for --post (refused for --pre), branch the not-published lead cause on success vs not-success, and order the job-summary verdict the same way.
2. Pass needs.publish.result from release.ymls provenance-post job into the new flag; update the script usage line and its header contract.

3. Update every --post invocation in test/release-provenance.test.ts; add a test pinning BOTH wordings (succeeded -> lag-led, not succeeded -> partial-publish-led) and the refusal of a missing/unknown/badly-valued flag.
4. bun test and bun run lore check exit 0; CHANGELOG Unreleased/Changed entry; docs runbook section re-read for wording that now differs.
5. Reviewer pass over the scripts/ + release.yml change (AC3); then complete on the branch citing PR + run id.
implementationNotes:
REVIEW PASS + FINAL EVIDENCE (2026-09-28, branch fix/LCLI-635-provenance-post-lead-cause). Head before the tracker-only completion commit: 0389cf72. Toolchain this proof resolved: bun 1.3.14, node v24.20.0, lore 0.11.0, quest 0.11.0; lore from source (bun run lore check), never the installed binary.

WHAT SHIPPED. scripts/release-provenance.mjs --post takes --publish-result (needs.publish.result passed through verbatim): REQUIRED there (exit 2 if absent), refused on --pre, and refused when the value is outside GitHub's success|failure|cancelled|skipped vocabulary. The not-published ::warning:: and the job summary's verdict both lead with the read-API lag (LCLI-460) when the result is success and with a partial publish otherwise, and the log names the value on every run. release.yml passes ${{ needs.publish.result }} as PUBLISH_RESULT; the workflow test pins the expression, not a literal.

GATES AT 0389cf72: bun test 4650 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail (130 files); bun run typecheck exit 0; bun run lint exit 0 (4 pre-existing warnings in files this change does not touch); bun run lore check 82 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.

REVIEWER PASS (opum-workflow:reviewer, dispatched on 3f5bdb51, AC3). Five findings, four fixed in 0389cf72. The reviewer ran all four values against the real registry and found the shipped classification CORRECT for each, so no live-behaviour defect was found; the findings were one test-strength gap, two prose clauses that named impossible failure modes, and a doc overstatement. Its own words for the shipped code: "The shipped code is correct".

- F1 (moderate, test strength): only success and failure were exercised, so a classifier written as != "failure" -- which prints the success wording, naming success, into a run whose log line says cancelled -- passed the ENTIRE suite (4647 tests, measured by the reviewer). FIXED: the partial branch is now a loop over failure, cancelled and skipped, each asserting its own value is named and success never is. MEASURED after the fix: that mutant reds 2 of 83 in this file (cancelled, skipped); the failure case correctly stays green because the mutant is right for that value.
- F2 (moderate-low): the order assertion compared uppercase literals, so the reviewer's mutant opening with "a partial publish is one way to reach this warning" passed 139/139. FIXED: the causes are matched case-insensitively by concept (causeIndex), the partial test also sets GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and asserts the summary's verdict, and the false claim that the two runs "differ only in the flag" is gone (the success run sets GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and the others did not). MEASURED: that mutant now reds 1 of 83 (the succeeded-wording test).
- F3 (low): "and so does any step after it" named a failure mode this repository cannot produce -- the read-back step is the publish job's LAST step. Reworded to the half that is true of release.yml (a content mismatch there does fail the job).
- F4 (low): "so it stopped before these went out" is unwarranted for a job cancelled after its launcher publish. Reachability is thin (skipped cannot reach the script at all -- provenance-post's if: skips it) but the sentence no longer asserts where the publish stopped.
- F5 (low, docs): the CHANGELOG said the result names "the cause that is actually possible" and that "only the publish job's own result says which one it is". Both overstate it: success is the only value that RULES OUT a partial publish; for the other three the publish job's log is what tells the two apart. The bullet and the runbook paragraph are corrected, folding in the reviewer's unranked note that a package satisfied by publish_or_skip's skip check was not necessarily published by this run.
- Reviewer's clean areas, recorded so they are not re-checked: the workflow wiring (expression, run line, and no second --publish-result anywhere), the refusal/injection behaviour (values carrying LF or %0A refused with the value escaped, and no forged line beginning ::error:: in any probe), no missed call sites repo-wide, and provenance-pre being unaffected (NOT_PUBLISHED is produced only on the post path).

MUTATION DISCIPLINE, recorded because one of these is the interesting kind. The two mutants quoted in 3f5bdb51's message were predicted subsets BEFORE running and both matched exactly (1 of 81 each): making the wording partial-led unconditionally, and dropping the required-flag rail. The reviewer's F1 mutant is the one the first pass missed: predicted subset of 2 of 83 came back as 2 of 83 (cancelled, skipped) -- a fix that was right, tested by assertions blind to the three values they never ran. Generalisable rule to keep: pin a discriminator over its VALUE SET, not over the two values that happen to be convenient.
finalSummary: provenance-post's not-published warning now leads with the cause the publish job's own result allows. scripts/release-provenance.mjs --post takes --publish-result (needs.publish.result, verbatim: success|failure|cancelled|skipped), REQUIRED there and refused on --pre; the warning and the job summary lead with the read-API lag (LCLI-460) on success and with a partial publish otherwise, and the log names the value every run. release.yml passes the expression, pinned by test. Reviewer pass (AC3) found the shipped classification correct for all four values and returned five findings -- a test-strength gap where a != "failure" classifier passed the whole suite (F1), an order assertion satisfiable by a lowercase narrative lead (F2), two prose clauses naming impossible failure modes (F3, F4) and a CHANGELOG overstatement (F5) -- all four actionable ones fixed in 0389cf72 and each re-measured by mutation. Gates at 0389cf72: bun test 4650/1 skip/0 fail, typecheck and lint clean, bun run lore check 82 files 0 errors.
